nodes.label: System flows
nodes.rationale: Paths the running application takes. The browser never waits inside the request while a large timetable or a large export is built.

nodes.label: Async job boundary
nodes.rationale: The browser never waits inside the request while a large timetable or a large export is built. The request inserts a row and returns. A worker finishes the job.

nodes.label: Sign-in flow
nodes.rationale: Opening the site calls GET /api/session. An anonymous visit to / or /login shows the student and teacher form, which posts to /login and accepts only Student or Teacher. An anonymous visit under /admin shows the admin form, which posts to /admin/login and accepts only Admin, Super Admin, or HOD. A failed sign-in is recorded as a failed login. A successful sign-in stores the account in the Flask session and writes a user_sessions row.

nodes.label: Opening a page
nodes.rationale: A sidebar link goes through page-access.ts. If the role and permission allow the path, the React page calls /api. The API checks the session, then the route permission or own-role check, then the service and MySQL. The page check and the API check are separate. Hiding a menu item does not replace the API permission check.

nodes.label: Invitation and registration
nodes.rationale: A staff account with permission to change users creates an invitation. The row stores a token, an expiry, and status pending. /register/<token> calls GET /api/register/<token>. The preview says the link is open, used, expired, or invalid, and does not return the email address or the token. An open invitation can capture a face photo and submit POST /register/<token>. Success marks the invitation used. A pending invitation whose expiry is in the past is shown as expired.

nodes.label: Timetable generation flow
nodes.rationale: The Generate screen posts to /api/timetable/generate for one class, every class in one course, or every allocated class capped at 1000. The request inserts a timetable_jobs row and returns the job id. The page polls GET /api/timetable/jobs/id every 2 seconds. A timetable-queue thread runs generate_timetable_for_class, and the next class starts only after the previous class commits. Only one generation job is queued or running at a time. A second request attaches to that job instead of starting another. Classes run one after another so a faculty member or a room is not booked twice. The worker is a daemon thread in the Flask process, not a separate queue service.

nodes.label: Export and report flow
nodes.rationale: Export or Queue report posts to /api/exports or /api/reports, inserts processed_reports as queued, and returns at once. An export-queue thread writes the CSV in chunks, marks the job completed, and stores the file under the reports directory. Download via GET /api/reports/id/download is allowed only when the job is completed, the file stays inside the reports storage directory, and the caller may export reports or is the person who queued that job and still has the source permission. The list response does not include the file path.

nodes.label: Attendance flow
nodes.rationale: Staff with the attendance permissions open /admin/attendance and call /api/attendance/.... A teacher opens /my-attendance and writes attendance only for their own lecture, using the signed-in faculty identity. A student opens /my-attendance and sees their own subject totals. Mobile attendance sync stays on /mobile-sync/v1 and does not use the browser session.

nodes.label: Startup work
nodes.rationale: On the first request, Flask checks that MySQL answers. Outside the test run it then starts a background pass that adds any missing composite indexes. Existing indexes are left in place. The timetable and export workers start when the first job of that kind is queued.
